usage: Used to get someone's attention, ask someone to repeat themselves, or politely ask someone to move. It is universally understood across the Levant and is appropriate in both formal and casual situations. When asking to physically pass by someone or excusing yourself to leave, '3an iznak' is often preferred.

variants.label: getting attention (to a man)
variants.note: Used to get a man's attention, such as a waiter or a stranger on the street.

variants.label: getting attention (to a woman)
variants.note: Used to get a woman's attention.

variants.label: asking to pass/leave (to a man)
variants.note: Used when you need to physically pass by a man or when excusing yourself to leave a gathering.

variants.label: asking to pass/leave (to a woman)
variants.note: The feminine form of asking to pass by or leave.

examples.english: Excuse me, where is the nearest pharmacy?
Excuse me, I didn't hear you.
